entries.name: Mail-merge batch automation
entries.scenario: A marketing workstation runs a Word mail-merge that shells out to cmd.exe to post-process recipient CSV files exported from the CRM.
entries.evidence: ParentImage is WINWORD.EXE and the child is cmd.exe, but the command line references the mail-merge tool path; events cluster during campaign windows and originate from marketing workstations only.
entries.tuning: Exclude the mail-merge tool's command-line pattern, scoped to the marketing OU. Revisit quarterly - if the tool is replaced, the exclusion should die with it.

entries.name: Legacy Excel reporting add-in
entries.scenario: An old line-of-business Excel add-in launches wscript.exe to render reports whenever finance opens specific workbooks.
entries.evidence: ParentImage is EXCEL.EXE and the child is wscript.exe with the same script path across events; a single finance user group is affected and the workbook filenames are report-related.
entries.tuning: Exclude the add-in's script path, and file a ticket to migrate the reporting - this is technical debt that should eventually be retired rather than permanently tuned out.

entries.name: Deployment script using Invoke-Expression
entries.scenario: A provisioning script legitimately downloads a configuration module and runs it via Invoke-Expression - matching the rule's DownloadString-plus-IEX pattern.
entries.evidence: CommandLine contains both DownloadString and IEX, but the URL points at the internal package mirror and the executing account is the deployment tool's service account.
entries.tuning: Exclude the internal mirror hostname for that service account only - never exclude the account itself. Give the exclusion an expiry date and prefer rewriting the script to avoid IEX.

entries.name: New jump host during a migration
entries.scenario: The infrastructure team builds a replacement RDP jump host and moves administrators to it over a weekend.
entries.evidence: Logon Type 10 succeeds from one new source IP, but the account is in the server-admins group, the destination hosts are the normal admin tier, and the change matches an approved change ticket.
entries.tuning: Add the new jump host to the approved_jump_hosts list, scoped to the admin group. Keep the rule active for non-admin accounts and external source ranges.

entries.name: Cloud VDI egress range change
entries.scenario: A VDI provider changes its NAT egress range, so every legitimate RDP session appears from a new address.
entries.evidence: Dozens of users and hosts shift to the same new range at once; the source range belongs to the VDI provider's published ASN.
entries.tuning: Allow the provider's published range for the VDI service account only; review the range quarterly and remove it on contract end.

entries.name: SCCM software deployment
entries.scenario: Configuration Manager installs a legitimate agent remotely and creates a short-lived service on the target.
entries.evidence: Service name is random-looking but the parent process is the SCCM agent, the binary is signed by the software vendor, and the install matches a deployment window.
entries.tuning: Exclude the SCCM service account and the deployment host only; do not exclude the service-name pattern globally.

entries.name: Break-glass account during an incident
entries.scenario: An on-call engineer uses the break-glass account from a hotel network after the normal SSO path fails.
entries.evidence: Console login without MFA from a new country, but the account is the documented break-glass identity, the session is short, and the ticket is open.
entries.tuning: Allow the break-glass account from the corporate travel range only during an approved incident; alert on every other use.

entries.name: Internal vulnerability scanner
entries.scenario: A scheduled scanner resolves common service names under the corporate zone as part of an asset inventory.
entries.evidence: The source is the scanner's fixed RFC1918 address, the query set matches its wordlist, and the scan window is on the approved schedule.
entries.tuning: Exclude the scanner IP for the inventory window, never the canary name. Any canary hit must still page.

entries.name: Portable support tool
entries.scenario: IT support runs a signed remote-support executable from a Downloads folder during a user session.
entries.evidence: Image is a signed vendor binary in Downloads, the parent is explorer.exe, and the user is in the support group with an open ticket.
entries.tuning: Exclude the signed binary hash for the support group, not the Downloads path. Prefer a managed install so the exception can be removed.
